src/auth/user.repository.ts: store(), login() and getUserForResetPassword() all save or look up UserEntity

parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The unit is one file, src/auth/user.repository.ts, with one class, UserRepository. That class extends BaseRepository<UserEntity, UserSerializer>. All of its methods deal with the user entity: store saves a user, login and getUserForResetPassword look users up, and transform/transformMany convert UserEntity to UserSerializer. That is one cohesive concern.

transform and transformMany replace the base class's methods of the same names using the same generic types. That uses the module's abstraction rather than going around it.

There are some concerns. login decides policy: it checks the password, requires status ACTIVE, and maps failures to ExceptionTitleList and StatusCodesList codes. store sets the default status (INACTIVE) and generates the password salt. getUserForResetPassword applies the rule that a reset token must still be valid. These are authentication rules that arguably belong in a service, not a repository.

However, I can't see the other files, so I can't show that any of these rules is repeated elsewhere, such as in JwtStrategy or AuthService. Within this file, each rule appears only once. The file does not split into unrelated concerns, and there is no shown bypass of BaseRepository. Questions about which layer this logic should live in are out of scope for this rule. Result: pass, with moderate confidence.
